observations: An isolated macOS home and disposable repository exercised installation, adoption, repeat sync, drift and conflict detection, uninstall restoration, and preservation of unrelated user configuration and skills.

Native responses changed from PLAIN to TAGGED after switching one custom proof-label stance. Session and project overrides resolved through the shared primitive authority, and built-in delegation and voice selections changed generated instructions and worker behavior without a separate Claude catalog.

Manual mode and an autonomy denial prevented disposable writes, while an explicitly acknowledged bypass created its sentinel. Claude Code 2.1.273 accepted the Auto selection but requires Sonnet 5 to retain native Auto Mode; the tested Bedrock account has zero Sonnet 5 runtime quota, so native Auto execution reported unavailable and created no write rather than silently widening permissions.
Native PostToolUse execution composed both per-path Review Card warnings for one multi-file change while retaining an independent user hook; hook trust was reviewed through the native client.
Isolated gatherer and planner workers completed under native read restrictions, and forced write attempts were denied while permitted reads succeeded. Planner publication remained parent-mediated.
The stop gate reused an unchanged green result, reran for staged, untracked, and edited-untracked changes, blocked a failing gate through its retry budget, and ended unverified without a green hash.
The full four-layer BMad review completed against the assigned implementation worktree, found both seeded defects, ran both resolvers, and preserved the implementation bytes.
A Claude to Codex to Claude handoff advanced revisions 1, 2, and 3, rejected stale state, demoted inherited verification to unverified, and transferred no approvals.
